bull.b: Improving revenue across the first half, supported by strong e-commerce and subscription adoption, indicates growing customer traction for SenesTech’s products. If sustained, this channel expansion can build a broader recurring revenue base and improve operating leverage as sales scale.

A 73.6% gross margin provides a stronger foundation for eventual profitability than the company’s prior performance. Continued margin improvement, aided by direct-channel economics, pricing discipline, and mix, could allow incremental revenue to contribute more meaningfully toward fixed operating costs.

Measured reduction in rodent activity supports the practical effectiveness of SenesTech’s non-lethal fertility-control approach within integrated pest management. Demonstrated outcomes can strengthen the product’s credibility with municipalities and commercial customers seeking longer-term population control.

bear.b: Large ongoing losses show that revenue and gross-margin gains have not yet translated into a self-sustaining operating model. Until sales growth outpaces operating costs, SenesTech remains exposed to continued earnings erosion and limited visibility on when the business can reach profitability.

Material cash consumption and an estimated nine-month funding runway constrain financial flexibility over the next several quarters. If operating momentum or margins weaken, the company may need additional capital before reaching positive cash generation, creating execution and financing pressure.

The timing and scale of larger institutional contracts remain uncertain, limiting confidence that B2B can become a dependable growth engine soon. Reliance on early traction and delayed wins makes the revenue outlook less predictable and may postpone the operating leverage needed to reduce losses.
